## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This pull request adds timeout parsing, port validation, JSON config loading, and hostname normalization. It also deletes a defaults file still required by startup and introduces several correctness, observability, documentation, and coverage issues.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file leaves `app.startup.load_defaults()` unconditionally reading a nonexistent path — Every call to load the application defaults now raises `FileNotFoundError`, preventing normal startup.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — The strict upper comparison rejects port `65535`, although the function documents the usable range as inclusive from 1 through 65535 — A valid service configured on TCP port 65535 is incorrectly rejected.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `load_config()` catches every `Exception` and returns `{}` without logging or signaling failures such as malformed JSON, an unreadable file, or a misspelled path — The application can silently continue with an empty configuration while concealing the actual configuration error.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says an empty hostname “returns None,” while the empty-input branch returns `""` — Callers following the documented contract cannot reliably distinguish an absent host from an empty string.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — The added hostname test covers lowercasing but never exercises the trailing-dot branch with an input such as `Example.COM.` — A regression that stops normalizing fully qualified hostnames would pass the test suite.

(none)

## Strengths
- The milliseconds timeout branch has a direct behavioral test.
- Valid JSON configuration loading and the lower port boundary are covered.
- The optional JSON accelerator has an explicit standard-library fallback.
